resources.string: Add the KuocKey keyboard in Settings
Tap above, then turn on KuocKey.
Choose KuocKey as the current keyboard
Tap here, pick KuocKey with the keyboard switcher, and type
Type an English word while in Vietnamese (or the other way round) and KuocKey fixes the word and switches. Press delete right after to undo.
When you press the VI/EN key yourself, KuocKey doesn\'t switch on its own for 5 seconds, so your choice sticks.
In web address, email and web search fields, KuocKey starts in English and goes back to your previous language when you leave the field.
Telex and Simple Telex 2: a lone w types ư. Simple Telex 1: a lone w stays w. In all three, uw, ow and aw type ư, ơ and ă. On the phone keyboard, [ and ] are always brackets.
Where the tone mark goes on oa, oe, uy: new style (hoà, thuý) or old style (hòa, thúy).
Only add tone marks when the word follows Vietnamese spelling rules.
When you finish a word that isn\'t valid Vietnamese, KuocKey puts back exactly the keys you typed.
Show suggested words above the keys, in both Vietnamese and English. Tap a word to use it.
When you hit a neighbouring key (\"teh\" instead of \"the\"), KuocKey fixes the word when you press space. Press delete right after to keep what you typed.
The first letter of a sentence is capitalized, like the system keyboard.
A light tap on every key, like the system keyboard. KuocKey never sends anything off your phone.
Double-tap the space bar to insert a period followed by a space.

Shows the time each key press takes, the number of haptics and the touches Android sends, above the keys, and writes them to a log. The log never contains what you type, only timings and the key kind (letter, space, delete…).
Nothing yet. Open the KuocKey keyboard and type something.

English and Vietnamese,\nswitched as you type
Type English in the middle of Vietnamese and KuocKey fixes the word and switches for you.
The keyboard never uses the network; what you type stays on your phone.
Tap the box below, pick KuocKey with the keyboard switcher, then try typing \"tooi ddi meeting nhes\".
KuocKey switches between English and Vietnamese using word statistics counted from these sources. The app contains only the statistics, never the text.
Used only to measure and improve accuracy; not in the app.
